objectives.text: Keep the Ouattara system: a fourth term won on 25 October 2025 with the two strongest rivals kept off the ballot. Thiam was removed from the electoral roll over his nationality, and Laurent Gbagbo was excluded after a criminal conviction; Simone Gbagbo stood. The provisional result gave Ouattara about 89.8% on turnout of about 50%, and the opposition called for new elections.

grand_strategy.reading: Abidjan's grand strategy is to keep the Ouattara system intact after the October 2025 election, won with the two strongest rivals barred, and to stay inside ECOWAS as the frame of its regional policy. Its security backing from France has been pared back (the Port-Bouet base passed to Ivorian control from January 2025), and the hostile neighbour is now Burkina Faso, whose junta accuses Abidjan of harbouring its destabilisers. Not verified for this card: the cocoa and Abidjan-port economy, the United States, China, the EU, Morocco, Ghana and Nigeria as stances, the CFA franc, JNIM attacks on the northern border, and the six officials' fate after September 2025.

stances.note: Traore accused Abidjan of welcoming Burkina's destabilisers in April 2024. In April 2025 the junta announced a foiled plot it blamed on masterminds in Ivory Coast (junta claim, AFP copy); in September 2025 the head of state named neighbouring countries, Ivory Coast among them. Rival is our reading (C): friction and mutual charges, with no sign of a will to destroy the other regime; no source uses the word. Abidjan rejects the charges and says Burkina has offered no proof. Trend cooling from the 2024 to 2025 escalation. Bond grievance is our reading (the accusations and the detentions as an open wound). Gaps: the six Ivorian officials reported detained in late August 2025 come from search summaries and are not confirmed at source (the allAfrica article returned HTTP 403); JNIM attacks on the northern border are not sourced here.

stances.note: Mali's junta held 46 Ivorian soldiers after their 2022 arrest (three women were freed in September 2022). A Bamako court gave them 20-year terms in late December 2022, and Goita pardoned the group in early January 2023. ECOWAS set Mali a deadline and did not impose sanctions. Abidjan said the men were a backup force for MINUSMA; Bamako called them mercenaries. Rival is our reading (C): a serious dispute with no sign of a will to destroy the other state; no source uses the word. Bond grievance is our reading of the trial as an open wound. Trend stable is a placeholder: no source after January 2023 was read, so the present direction is a gap. Gap: bilateral relations since 2023 are not researched.

stances.note: Abidjan announced at the end of 2024 that French forces would leave; the Port-Bouet base passed to Ivorian control from January 2025 (AllAfrica, 1 January 2025). Partner is our reading (C): the military leg is ending while language and monetary ties remain. No source read here calls the relation a partnership, and none uses the word. Not ally: no treaty or defence guarantee was read here, so any defence agreement and its status remain unverified. Bond affinity is our reading: shared francophone and colonial history, with no grievance named in the sources read. Trend cooling from the basing exit. Gaps: the exact handover day is not in the source read; the CFA franc and any post-handover French presence are not sourced here.
